## Architecture

RUST (u1): crates/store/migrations/0012_seat_harness_session.sql (nullable TEXT harness_session), crates/store/src/migrate.rs SCHEMA_VERSION 11→12 (CONVERGENCE: s122 lands 0011/10→11 on branch s122/tmux-full-body — rebase onto whichever is on main; second lander reconciles), SeatDescriptor gains harness_session: Option<String> (crates/core model + store row mapping), registration (crates/daemon/src/registration.rs register(), identity.rs caller struct :84-100 — add a generic `harness_session`/HARNESS_SESSION_ID alias the pi/omp extension sends; claude/copilot keep their existing aliases and map into the same column), projections in /v1/seats and state. TS (u2): generation-routing row for `sessions` → `/v1/shim/sessions` (mirror the s119 `send`/`inbox check` rows in .pi/extensions/pij/core/generation-routing.ts + adapters/generation-router.ts; requiresSeatInRs is NOT required for a read-only union — route whenever rs answers); the shim handler in crates/daemon/src/http/shim.rs returns rs rows; the TS side merges buildSessionJoinRows (cli.ts:2926-2960) + rs rows → frozen shape; whoami --json: generation-routing.ts currently refuses E-RS by design (see its message) — replace with the named-absent-gate shape; the extension registration (adapters/rust-runtime.ts:85-98 registrationFor + core/daemon-wire.ts Registration) sends harness_session from index.ts:328 piSessionId. Fakes: existing daemon test world + FakeRegistry; TS seam tests already cover routing rows (generation-seam.test.ts).

## Isolation

| mode | worktree-per-coder off the plan branch (~/pi-hacking/fs3-seat-session-identity, 128-seat-session-identity); PM composes |
| note | Default: each coder gets its own worktree, branching off the PM's plan branch; unit lands back onto the plan branch (PM merges — coders never merge). Shared-tree work is the retro-proven #1 hazard (staged sweeps, untrustworthy greens) — only choose it for trivially disjoint single-wave work, and then file-scoped `git add` only, never -A. REMEMBER: fences partition WRITE intent, not the build — a mid-refactor sibling can still break your compile, so waves must respect build dependencies, and a broken workspace build is a PM composition concern, not a coder's to fix cross-fence. |
